title: Republican Setbacks Swell in the South With Stinging Loss in Mississippi
summary: The Democrat Scott Colom’s stunning Senate upset punctuated a dismal midterm showing for the G.O.P. in a region they had dominated for years.

Republicans were routed in Georgia and stunned in South Carolina. In Louisiana, a Republican Senate candidate won by less than two percentage points against a little-known Democrat who ran just two TV commercials.


Then came Wednesday in Mississippi, where Scott Colom[became the first Democrat to win a Senate race in 44 years](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/us/elections/mississippi-senate-colom-hyde-smith.html) , defeating Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith and further shaking Republicans’ once-unquestioned hold on the South.


Now, after the series of midterm shocks, Southern Republicans have been left to confront a new reality: A region they dominated for years is no longer a lock for their party.


“Republicans fell asleep at the wheel,” said Bill Armistead, a former chair of the Alabama Republican Party, adding, “If we stay asleep at the wheel, we could see some losses in the future.”


Image


Ms. Hyde-Smith’s loss cast doubts on Republicans’ once-unquestioned power in the South.


Credit...


Michael A. McCoy for The New York Times


Republicans also lost their grip on the Georgia governor’s mansion, suffered a staggering loss by nearly 20 points in[North Carolina’s Senate race](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/11/03/us/elections/results-north-carolina-us-senate.html) and surrendered seats in state houses in Tennessee, Alabama and Arkansas. In South Carolina, 10 state legislative seats flipped into Democratic hands.
